clauses.reason: The authorization continues, amended. Before the amendment the clause authorized the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation with respect to members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations; after EO 13286 section 62 (effective March 1, 2003) the Coast Guard officer is the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the rest of the clause, including the Secretary of State concurrence for determinations, is unchanged. The U.S. Code note prints the order in that amended form, and no held instrument revokes or supersedes it, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14. The substance of the clause is unchanged by the amendment; only the named officer changed.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11446 of January 16, 1969 (34 FR 803), Authorizing the Acceptance of Service Medals and Ribbons from Multilateral Organizations Other Than the United Nations, is a single paragraph. The President authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of Transportation (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations, and requires that a determination that service for such an organization is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619, 10629), section 62, amends the order by striking the words the Secretary of Transportation and inserting the words the Secretary of Homeland Security; section 92 of that order states that it becomes effective on March 1, 2003, so the amendment took effect on March 1, 2003. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor, but its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11446, and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so I do not treat EO 12977 as a later event. The OFR executive-order catalog lists only the amendment by EO 13286. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 13286 section 62, as a note to 5 U.S.C. 7342 with no ending statement. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation, supersession or other amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
